title: Quant artifact fingerprint registry and recovery procedure
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Calibration outputs (FP8/INT8 profiles, calibration traces, goldenset evals) are currently stored ad-hoc. Small non-functional changes (logging, rounding stochasticity, ordering) produce artifacts that are hard to compare, causing uncertainty when promoting quant artifacts to production. We need a deterministic, verifiable registry for quant artifacts with a compact fingerprint, an auditable signed ledger, and a clear recovery procedure so engineers can reproduce, validate, and (if needed) revert to a known-good artifact without rebuilding from scratch under time pressure.

This ticket proposes: (1) a canonicalization + fingerprint scheme for quant artifacts (calibration manifests, profile blobs, calibration seed/generator state, goldenset digest, quant tool version); (2) an immutable registry index (fingerprint -> object store path + metadata) with optional signed ledger entries; (3) verification and replay checks integrated into CI and production rollout gates; (4) a fast recovery procedure to mark and route away from suspect artifacts and rehydrate previous artifacts with minimal downtime. The design emphasizes reproducibility, human-auditable provenance, and low operational friction for rollbacks and audits.
acceptance_criteria: Define a canonical manifest schema and canonicalization rules that remove non-deterministic fields and enforce ordering for lists.
Fingerprint computed as SHA-256(hex) over the canonical manifest + calibration RNG state + goldenset digest + quant-tool version; example fingerprint format: sha256:<hex>.
Registry API: post artifact -> returns fingerprint; get artifact by fingerprint -> returns signed URL or object path and metadata; list returns optional release tags.
Ledger signing: Ed25519 signatures supported; KMS-backed signing for enterprise customers; signature metadata stored alongside artifact metadata.
CI verifies fingerprints by re-hydrating artifact from object store and running deterministic replay of calibration harness on a subset (goldenset) with metric tolerances defined in metadata.
Rollback workflow documented and executable with a single CLI command: redwood-quant recover --fingerprint <fp> --target-pool <pool>.
Telemetry emitted for fingerprint creation, verification failures, and recovery events; dashboards updated in Console for SLO/quality regressions.
Security review completed and KMS signing integration validated on a staging tenant.
End-to-end test in CI that reproduces an INT8 quant artifact from source checkpoint and verifies fingerprint matches registry entry.
implementation_notes: Canonicalization rules: remove timestamps, normalize float text formats, sort lists deterministically, and record quant-tool git SHA and pip package versions.
Fingerprint input components: canonical_manifest.json + calibration_rng_state.bin (base64) + goldenset_digest.txt + quant_tool_version.txt.
Use SHA-256(hex) over the concatenated inputs with clear separators; prefix fingerprint with 'sha256:' to allow future algorithm swaps.
Registry backend: extend existing artifacts S3 bucket with /quant-registry/<fingerprint>/ metadata.json and signed ledger entries in DynamoDB for quick lookup.
Signing: support both ephemeral CI signing (for internal) and KMS/enterprise signing (customer keys stored in KMS). Ledger entry includes signature, signer-id, and cert chain URL.
CI gating: create a small deterministic replay harness (1000 tokens goldenset) for quick verification; full goldenset runs scheduled nightly for regression detection.
On-disk artifact layout: store calibration profile, KV-cache samples (first N tokens), quant config JSON, and a reproducible seed snapshot (rng state), each referenced from manifest by sha256.

Delta-indexing: allow optional 'delta' pointers between fingerprints when only metadata changes (e.g., labels); deltas are not allowed to change numeric calibration outputs without producing a new fingerprint and failing CI.
Backward compatibility: accept legacy artifacts by producing a compatibility manifest that lists original fields and a generated canonical manifest (marked as derived).
Performance: fingerprint computation should be < 5s for typical artifacts; parallelize component hashing and stream from S3 to avoid full downloads.
Dev ergonomics: provide 'redwood-quant show <fingerprint>' to print human-friendly provenance and 'redwood-quant verify <fingerprint>' to run the CI replay locally.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement canonicalizer + fingerprint generator and run on historical artifacts to validate determinism (week 1).
Phase 2 (CI integration): add fingerprint verification step to quant CI pipelines; block merges that change fingerprinted artifacts without a manifest update (week 2).
Phase 3 (registry): deploy registry storage and ledger with signing and KMS integration; migrate new artifacts to registry; create Console UI for fingerprint lookup (week 3).
Phase 4 (canary): route 10% of model traffic to variants using registry-backed artifacts with replay verification at deploy time; monitor accuracy deltas and rollback needs (week 4).
Phase 5 (full): require fingerprint registration for all promoted quant artifacts and deprecate ad-hoc artifacts after one full cycle (week 6).
rollback_procedure: Identification: Console or alert identifies a regression linked to fingerprint sha256:<hex>.
Verification: run 'redwood-quant verify <fingerprint>' to confirm artifact integrity; check ledger signature and goldenset replay results.

Recovery: run 'redwood-quant recover --fingerprint <fallback-fp> --target-pool <pool>' which: (a) updates model routing to point to fallback artifact, (b) emits event to telemetry and audit log, (c) triggers a background rehydrate job for the problematic pool.
Post-recovery: mark the offending fingerprint as deprecated in registry and start a rebuild/recalibration jenkins job with the exact canonical manifest recorded in the ledger.
Communication: post incident note linking fingerprint, ledger entry, and PRs; notify product and SRE channels with remediation status.
Graceful fallback policy: if fallback fingerprint is older than X days, require manual approval unless metric delta < configured threshold.
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer (ordering, field stripping, numeric normalization).
Property tests: fuzzy inputs produce identical canonical manifests when semantically equivalent.
Integration test: end-to-end reproduce artifact from checkpoint -> compute fingerprint -> registry store -> CI verify reproduces fingerprint.
Load test: bulk fingerprint computation on 10k artifacts to validate registry indexing and S3 interaction patterns.
Security test: signing verification with compromised key scenario and KMS rotation test.
Chaos test: simulate partial object store failure and validate recovery flow handles missing components gracefully.
